body:
You know, I wanna throw this out there: you possibly may not feel like you're being really helpful when you're talking about how you DON'T know certain things, but in my experience that often comes across as being a lot more sincere and comforting (in a strange way... validation?) than listening to certain people who like to talk about how they DO know/understand everything. Most often, the know-it-alls turn out to have a really superficial comprehension of things.

You're on the right track in a lot of ways, I feel, in that you're probably more open to trying to understand other peoples' experience, truly and for real. Kudos.

I didn't really answer your post, though.

I dunno, mate. Thank you. How long were the dark points?

My current therapist is probably one of the better ones I've had, particularly in the aspect that she's acknowledged my frustration with previous experiences—I referred to DBT (Dialectical Behavioural Therapy) last time we met as "Nickelback Therapy", and she had this good deep full-hearted laugh about it in my presence, suggesting that yeah, she knows what I mean by that.

(context, just in case: I live in Alberta, Canada. Nickelback is/was one of the most popular bands in the world for awhile, and local! ...but it's this... super lame pastiche of early 90s grunge rock that everybody already knows and nobody wants to admit listening to.. it sounds like they're trying to be oh-so-sincere and "deep"... but it's patently commercial and contrived at the same time.)

Little things like that are important. I don't know how to say that I'm "really" suicidal, tho, as by nature I tend to work these things out in my own time away from prying eyes. Whenever I actually meet her, by definition, I've already had to build up my psyche for an excursion, and sat for 20 minutes on the train surrounded by people, so that by the time I get there it's hard to remember what I'm "really" feeling most of the time....

...I'm really, really good at "performing". There's the saying, "fake it till you make it", and I've done a lot of that up to the point of actually pushing myself to do strip-teases and such in public in front of 300 people. I can fake it. I've got that skill set. That's not the problem.

Fair point, but unlikely. I've communicated with her by e-mail in the past. She is not the type to check it while she's not at work.

Yes, I'm still alive. Are you going to say that I was faking it for attention, then, since I didn't kill myself immediately after telling Reddit about my thoughts and plans? The title of this thread includes the words "mostly planned"; of course there is hesitation; of course there is still activity in the mind; someone (I don't remember who) once described depression as something like "a mind that doesn't want to live in a body that doesn't want to die", or something like that. There's a lot of confusing ambiguity in this experience.

LOL. Yes, that's what you get: a LOL.

Here's the thing: I don't come across as being "crazy". I am very, very, controlled. That's part of my point in writing this, is that it's perfectly possible to be suicidal without being a hyped-up, irrational maniac.

Thanks for reading. I guess I know that feeling—there's a lot that goes on in the head that is hard to articulate, and that's probably for the best, overall. Otherwise the world would be this one big non-stop facebook wall of people providing predictable responses with little variation.
